subject: Vendor portal onboarding: OneTrust crosswalk and evidence escrow
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <security@greenbank.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor portal onboarding: OneTrust crosswalk + escrow question

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for taking this — Greenbank is kicking off procurement for the inference layer and we need to onboard Redwood into our vendor portal (OneTrust). A couple of asks from our side to unblock the security review: 

- Can you confirm who at Redwood will be the profile owner in OneTrust during onboarding and whether you support temporary evidence escrow (signed manifest + S3 staging) while procurement completes?
- We need SOC 2 Type II artifact access (last 12 months) plus a snapshot of relevant CAIQ/SIG answers.
- If you also integrate with Whistic or Vendr, could you provide the outbound contact and any service-account patterns we should expect?

I've attached a short checklist of the docs we need to accept the vendor profile. If you can confirm a proposed timeline and the contact that will accept our SSO invite, we can provision portal access today.

Attachments: greenbank_evidence_checklist.xlsx (stub)

Regards,
Alex Mercer
Senior Security Manager — Third-Party Risk
Greenbank Financial
security@greenbank.com
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <security@greenbank.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor portal onboarding: OneTrust crosswalk + escrow question

Alex — thanks for the checklist and the clear asks. Tiny plan below; happy to adjust if you have constraints.

Summary plan
- Owner: I (Evelyn Hart, Head of Platform Security) will accept the OneTrust invite and act as temporary profile owner during procurement.
- Evidence escrow: Redwood can provision a read-only S3 staging bucket and supply a signed escrow manifest (PDF) that enumerates uploaded artifacts. We typically create a service-account for the portal ingestion team and add a short-lived presign policy for uploads.
- Artifacts: SOC 2 report (redacted), CAIQ export (JSON + human-readable PDF), sample logs for retention proof.

Requested from you
- Please confirm which identity you sent the invite to (email).
- Any specific field-level mapping you require in OneTrust (we can run a crosswalk).

Proposed timeline
- Today: accept invite + walk Greenbank through the minimal evidence bundle (SOC2 redacted + CAIQ snapshot).
- +48 hours: S3 staging + signed escrow manifest uploaded; we will share presigned URLs and manifest hash.

Next steps I will take now
1) Accept OneTrust invite (if received) and create a temporary profile owner role.
2) Coordinate with Monica for the escrow manifest and with Rohan to provision a service-account.
3) Share links and manifest once uploaded.

If it helps, Monica will draft the minimal manifest template and loop in Vendr/Whistic contacts for inbound ingestion.

— Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Platform Security, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 08:48:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: escrow manifest and role signoff (Greenbank)

Eve / Rohan — looping internally with a few operational questions before we provide the manifest to Greenbank: 

- Who signs the escrow manifest on Redwood's side? We can have a delegated signatory (legal), or we can sign programmatically from a service-account with HMAC and include the key fingerprint in the manifest. Recommend the latter for faster turnaround.
- Suggested service-account: vendor-portal-escrow@redwood-inference.svc with read-only S3 presign scope and a 72-hour TTL for presigned URLs.
- I attached a first-pass escrow-manifest-v1.docx. It enumerates artifacts, SHA256 hashes, bucket paths, and the presign TTL. Please review for compliance.

Operational ask for Rohan: can you provision the service-account and a minimal IAM policy that we can hand to OneTrust/Vendr? I want the policy to avoid list/delete permissions — only PutObject (with ACL enforcement) + GetObject for ingestion.

Thanks — Monica
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: escrow manifest and role signoff (Greenbank)

Monica — can do. Confirming operational details: 

- Service account: vendor-portal-escrow@redwood-inference.svc (created).
- IAM policy: PutObject, GetObject, GetObjectAcl on bucket redwood-evidence-staging-greenbank; no List/Delete. Presigned URLs will be generated by our upload lambda.
- TTL: 72 hours for presigns; manifest will include presign expiry timestamps and the manifest hash signed with our HMAC key 'escrow-key-v2'.

Naomi — can you rotate a short-lived HMAC key for 'escrow-key-v2' and share the key-id so Monica can add the fingerprint to the manifest?

I'll also draft the minimal policy document to hand to OneTrust/Vendr so they know the upload flow.

— Rohan
From: Alex Mercer <security@greenbank.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor portal onboarding: OneTrust crosswalk and evidence escrow

Evelyn / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the plan. A few quick confirmations before we proceed: 

- Invite: I sent the OneTrust invite to evelyn_hart@redwood.com this morning — I see you accepted.
- Links: please share the OneTrust profile link and the HubSpot deal id once you have them. We also prefer the manifest to include the HMAC key fingerprint and presign expiry (both are in scope).
- For Whistic/Vendr ingestion: we accept the service-account pattern you outlined; please send contact addresses for the intake connector and a sample role-policy.

I'll take a quick pass on the escrow-manifest-v1 once Monica uploads it. Attached is our SLA exceptions tracker for reference.

Attachments: sla-exceptions-greenbank.pdf (stub)

Appreciate it — Alex
